summary: This class defines a decorated cookie that builds on an existing Cookie class. It reuses everything Cookie already knows how to do, and replaces the description with one that mentions sprinkles and icing.

lines.text: The `extends` keyword makes DecoratedCookie a specialized kind of Cookie, so it inherits the fields and methods Cookie already defines instead of repeating them.
A subclass does not inherit constructors, so DecoratedCookie needs its own that accepts the same flavor a plain Cookie would.
This calls the Cookie constructor to store the flavor, which is how the inherited part of the object gets set up before any subclass work happens.
This annotation tells the compiler you mean to replace a method inherited from Cookie; if the name or signature does not match, you get an error instead of a silently unused method.
Redefining describe() here means any DecoratedCookie uses this version, even when the code holding it only knows it as a Cookie.

lines.code: return "This " + getFlavor() + " cookie is decorated with sprinkles and icing!";
lines.text: The flavor is read through the inherited getter rather than the field directly, which is what keeps Cookie's data private and still usable.
